incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: Latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate in us-east-1. p95=820ms, p99=2.9s over last 5m. Increased streaming stalls observed. Severity: Sev2. Pager: oncall-eng. Links: https://metrics.redwood.internal/s/latency?svc=generate

lee: On it. Affected models? any correlation with model variant or quantization?

maria: Seeing correlation with continuous-batching path. Most high-latency samples show mixed sequence lengths shoved into same batch, long seqs causing stall on KV cache flush. Pulling traces now.

sahil: Confirmed. Trace sample: request_id=a9f3b2, sequence_lengths=[16,1024,64], batch_size=32, scheduler queued long seq behind many small ones. Streaming chunks stalled at token 512 then resumed -> stall ~1.8s.

caroline: Quick mitigation proposals: 1) reduce max batch size for continuous path to limit tail cost, 2) enable scheduling fairness (round-robin across sequence length buckets), 3) route long sequences to dedicated long-seq workers. Which can we flip fast?

lee: Can we flip #1 and #2 via runtime flags? If so do it as a scoped runbook change and watch p99.

maria: Yes. Runtime flags exist. Patch: 
```
rbctl set serving.continuous_batching.max_batch_size=8 --env us-east-1
rbctl set serving.continuous_batching.enable_fair_scheduling=true --env us-east-1
```
I can roll that in 60s. Expect throughput drop but should cut p99 tails.

sahil: Also recommend enabling aggressive prefix caching eviction for long sequences to avoid KV blowup: 
```
rbctl set serving.kv_cache.max_entries_per_request=128
```
But that needs validation for correctness.

caroline: Do the quick flags first. @maria please proceed. Notify if any downstream errors. :thumbsup:

maria: Rolling now to us-east-1. Will patch one AZ at a time. Starting AZ-1...

ops-bot: deploy-started: patch-serving-ct-batching-1753012392 by maria in us-east-1 AZ-1

maria: AZ-1 done. p99 dropped from 2.9s -> 1.1s in AZ-1. Streaming stalls reduced. Rolling AZ-2...

lee: Nice. Keep an eye on request queue growth and CPU on the small workers — reducing batch size can increase per-token CPU.

sahil: Observed slight increase in CPU and token cost, throughput steady. Taking a sample for 30m to validate.

caroline: Customer impact assessment: We see ~0.6% of total requests hit p99>2s during the incident window. About 12 active customers reported visible streaming stalls (mostly interactive chat sessions). Two enterprise customers opened support tickets referencing stalls affecting UX. No data loss.

lee: Next steps medium-term: 1) implement sequence-length-aware batching (split batches by length buckets), 2) create a long-seq worker pool autoscaled for low QPS but better parallelism, 3) add live alert for streaming-stalls (missing token deltas >500ms).

maria: Filed follow-up tasks: RD-1789 add length-aware batching to runtime, RD-1790 long-seq worker pool, RD-1791 streaming-stalls alert + dashboard.

ops-bot: ticket-created RD-1790 by maria
ops-bot: ticket-created RD-1791 by maria

lee: Handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. @sahil please take next on-call handoff for the night. Watch p99/us-east-1 and enterprise customer tickets. If p99 > 3s or stalls >= 0.8% escalate to Sev1.

sahil: Taking handoff. Will monitor dashboards and errors. Subscribed to alerts.

caroline: Post-incident notes: Root cause: continuous batching scheduler unfairly mixing very long sequences with many short ones; long seqs lock execution and cause streaming stalls at the tail. Immediate mitigation: reduced max_batch_size and enabled fairness. Impact: user-visible stalls for a small percent of traffic and a handful of customers. Next steps prioritized.

maria: Will add a small canary job to simulate mixed workloads to catch regressions. Also adding p99-by-seq-length metric in the console.

lee: Thanks team. Closing the active page but keeping thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
